$comment: Generated by orchestrator/backend/scripts/generate_agent_schemas.py from app.api.assessment.FindingRecordRequest plus agent-side overlays where the CLI contract is intentionally stricter than the backend model.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this finding (e.g. 'sqli-search-q'). Omit to auto-generate.

title.title: Title
title.description: One-line finding name: vuln class + location (e.g. 'Blind SQL injection in /search?q').

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: CVSS-aligned impact rating. Use 'critical' only for CVSS >=9.0 or trivially exploitable RCE/auth-bypass.

workflow_status.title: Workflow Status
workflow_status.description: Lifecycle state settable at record time. New findings: 'active'. Post-exploitation confirmed: 'exploited'. WAF/control stopped testing: 'blocked'. Duplicate absorbed into another record: 'merged'. Delivered to client: 'reported'. NOTE: the blue-team/IR states (contained, eradicated, recovered) are intentionally NOT recordable here — they are applied only via `vigil assess finding update`, so this finding record enum is deliberately narrower than the full WorkflowStatus vocabulary.

verification_status.title: Verification Status
verification_status.description: Shared verification state on a stored finding record. New API writes still start at 'unreviewed'; `vigil assess finding verify` owns transitions to disputed, pending_runtime_proof, blocked, confirmed, downgraded, or false_positive and enforces their evidence gates.

defect_family.title: Defect Family
defect_family.description: Short vuln-class label for grouping (e.g. 'sql-injection', 'buffer-overflow', 'ssrf'). Use kebab-case.

root_cause_key.title: Root Cause Key
root_cause_key.description: Stable key linking variants to a shared root cause (e.g. 'missing-input-sanitization-search'). Omit if not part of a variant cluster.

auth_context.title: Auth Context
auth_context.description: Authentication state when the finding was triggered. Use 'anonymous', a role name (e.g. 'user', 'admin'), or credential slug.

canonical_location.title: Canonical Location
canonical_location.description: Primary affected location. URL for network findings (e.g. 'https://target.example/search?q'); 'file:path:line' for code findings.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Concise submission-quality Markdown (normally 2-5 sentences): what is vulnerable, how it is triggered, and the concrete attacker impact.

evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref
evidence_ref.description: Path or identifier for supporting artifact (e.g. 'scans/sqlmap.txt', 'artifacts/burp-export.xml'). Leave empty if evidence is inline in details.evidence.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Operational replay log in readable Markdown. Use short sections or a numbered sequence and fenced code blocks for exact commands, requests, responses, and tool output. Keep submission narrative in details; notes are not shown in reports.

source_name.title: Source Name
source_name.description: Agent or tool that produced this record (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst', 'nuclei'). Mirrors provenance.agent_name for quick filtering.

discovered_by.description: Agent name that first identified this finding (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst').

owasp_category.description: OWASP Top 10 2021 category code and name (e.g. 'A03:2021 Injection').

cwe_id.description: CWE identifier (e.g. 'CWE-89' for SQL injection, 'CWE-122' for heap buffer overflow).

parameter.description: Exact name of the affected input: query param, header, JSON key, or form field (e.g. 'q', 'X-User-Id', 'username').

slot_type.description: Code-analysis input class for the attack (e.g. 'URL-COMPONENT', 'NETWORK-INPUT', 'PROTOCOL-FIELD').

request_method.description: HTTP verb that triggers the finding (e.g. 'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE').

evidence.description: Authored Markdown explaining how the proof establishes the finding. Use short headings when several observations are present and fenced code blocks for exact commands, requests, responses, or tool output; put large raw captures in an artifact or poc_request/poc_response instead. Preserve quoted evidence bytes verbatim and include enough context to reproduce independently.

kill_reason.description: Verifier rationale for false_positive verdict: which check failed and why the issue is not exploitable.

kill_check.description: Verification check number (1-5) that produced the false-positive verdict.

entry_point.description: Where attacker-controlled data enters the program (e.g. 'curl_url_set(CURLURLPART_URL, attacker_url)', 'POST /upload body field filename').

sink.description: Dangerous operation that consumes tainted data (e.g. 'memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen) at lib/urlapi.c:342', 'sqlite3_exec(db, query)').

taint_path.description: Arrow-delimited data flow from entry_point to sink (e.g. 'curl_url_set -> parseurl() -> memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen)').

guards_evaluated.description: List each relevant bounds/validation check and state whether it is absent, bypassable, or ineffective (e.g. 'No bounds check on schemelen before memcpy').

ghsa.description: GitHub private advisory form metadata; credits are assigned by maintainers, not claimed by the reporter.

impact.description: Submission-quality Markdown stating the concrete attacker outcome, what data or action is exposed, and who is affected (e.g. 'Anonymous attacker can read all DB rows', 'Remote code execution via heap corruption').

cvss_vector.description: Complete CVSS v3.1 or v4.0 base vector; the CVSS:3.1/ or CVSS:4.0/ prefix declares the version. Threat, temporal, environmental, and supplemental metrics are not accepted.

cvss_score.description: CVSS v3.1 or v4.0 base score (0.0-10.0). Must match cvss_vector using its declared version.

remediation.description: Submission-quality Markdown naming the specific fix and missing control (e.g. 'Use parameterized queries', 'Add bounds check on schemelen before memcpy').

steps_to_reproduce.description: Authored Markdown with ordered reproduction steps, starting from initial access state and ending at impact observation. Preferred form is ONE string with explicit 1./2./… numbering, blank lines between complex steps, and fenced code blocks for commands, requests, or responses. Write FROM WHAT YOU ACTUALLY RAN, with concrete values (the real session cookie, object id, and payload), and preserve those values verbatim through submission. An unbound placeholder is a step nobody can follow; a list of strings remains accepted for legacy/simple records.

repro_runs.description: Command-run ids (from `vigil assess command-run list`) that actually produced this reproduction, in step order. Newly authored ids must resolve in this engagement; legacy missing ids are reported as advisories. `export submission` fetches each row and renders its real argv under OPERATOR DETAILS, so the reproduction is transcribed rather than paraphrased.

attack_scenario.description: Realistic adversary, starting access, and action, ending at first compromise. Renders as the submission's Attack Scenario section; omit when the reproduction already carries the narrative.

poc_code.description: Minimal exploit code or script that reproduces the finding. Omit if poc_request/poc_response is sufficient.

references.description: CVE IDs, NVD/advisory URLs, or CWE links relevant to this finding.

chain_required.description: Set true only when this finding has no standalone impact and is meaningful only as part of an exploit chain.

chain_rationale.description: REQUIRED (enforced on write, and by this schema) when chain_required is true: explain which chain step this enables and why standalone impact is insufficient.

required_followup.description: Concrete next steps needed to validate or complete the chain (e.g. 'Confirm reachable network caller for the URL parser').

precondition_analysis.description: Conditions required for exploitation and evidence establishing whether each condition is attacker-reachable.

severity_ceiling.description: Program- or precondition-derived upper bound on severity, including the reason for the cap when structured.

root_cause_candidates.description: Candidate shared causes considered during deduplication or grouping.

notes_provenance.description: Attribution for lifecycle-repair or analysis notes without changing the finding's discovery source.

roe_blocked.description: Set true when the primitive is proved but the program's rules of engagement forbid the final proof step; grade at impact-if-true. Distinct from a provisioning/access wall (see block_reason) and from chain_required (which needs another bug).

vrt_category.description: Bugcrowd VRT category for this finding (e.g. 'broken_access_control.idor'). Overridden by the --vrt-category flag on export.

weakness.description: HackerOne weakness for this finding (e.g. 'CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key'). Overridden by the --weakness flag on export; falls back to cwe_id.

crash_input.description: Path to the minimized crash input that reproduces the fault.

asan_report.description: ASAN/UBSAN summary line identifying the fault class and location.

attacker_trace.description: Full byte-to-crash trace: how attacker-controlled input reaches the faulting operation.

caller_feasibility.description: Which real entry points reach this code path, and under what conditions.

fp_gates.description: Results of every false-positive gate applied to this crash, so a reviewer sees which gates passed rather than a bare verdict.

campaign_id.description: Identifier of the fuzzing campaign that produced this crash.

fuzzer_confirmation.description: True when a fuzzer reproduced this finding, distinguishing it from a static-only inference.

attacker_access_path.description: How a real attacker obtains the disclosed bytes. Severity must follow this access path.

exposure_prerequisite.description: The concrete condition that gives a real attacker the bytes (e.g. 'file is served from a public S3 path', 'confirmed LFI reads this path').

bounded_or_systemic.description: Whether the observed impact is bounded to one object/tenant or systemic across them. Record the verdict when it is established — it cannot be reconstructed later.

credential_id.description: Identifier of the captured credential row this finding's PoC depends on, so a chain prerequisite stays traceable.

related_intel_ids.description: Identifiers of intel rows enriched from this finding's indicators.

disposition.description: Incident-response disposition in the blue vocabulary, carried for the report-writer.

mitre_techniques.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs (e.g. 'T1078') this finding maps to. Required on a blue-engagement finding before report readiness passes.

confidence.description: Stated confidence in the finding's disposition, paired with severity_rationale. Single-signal triage is `low` by definition.

severity_rationale.description: One-line justification for the assigned severity, per the impact-based severity model in agent/rules/triage.md.

severity_band_rationale.description: Why the assigned severity band DIVERGES from the band the CVSS base score implies (e.g. business context the vector cannot express). Present and non-empty demotes report-readiness' severity_cvss_mismatch blocker to an advisory; it never excuses the two CVSS-arithmetic blockers.

honest_bounds.description: What this finding does NOT establish — the limits of the evidence, stated by the author so a reader cannot over-read the claim.

intent_basis_caveat.description: Caveat on any inference about the target's intent or design rationale, naming what is observed versus what is assumed.

scope_metric_note.description: Qualification of a count or coverage figure cited by this finding (what the denominator is, and what it excludes).

self_obtainability_verdict.description: Whether the attacker can obtain the required precondition themselves ('self'), needs a victim action, or needs a privilege they cannot acquire.

mechanism_verdict.description: Adjudicated verdict on the proposed mechanism after review — what the mechanism actually is, versus what it was first believed to be. Undated: the transition ledger, not a date-stamped key, carries when it was written.

block_reason.description: Why the finding cannot be advanced right now — a provisioning/access wall blocking the next proof step (as opposed to an ROE policy wall or a missing-bug chain park). Surfaced in the resume-brief Attempts ledger.

unblock_requirements.description: What must be provisioned to lift the block so the finding can be driven to proof. When the unblocker is another finding or chain, link it with `vigil assess finding link <slug> --link-kind unblocked_by ...`.

kind.description: Category of what is needed: account | line | device | credential | access.

description.description: Concretely what to provision (e.g. 'a test account in the org-admin group with role-management entitlement').

requested_from.description: Who can provide it (e.g. 'program contact', 'target admin').

attempts_summary.description: One-line summary of what was tried and the result, for the resume-brief Attempts ledger (e.g. 'anonymous + member + billing-admin sessions all 403 at the function gate').

variant_of.description: Slug of the root finding when this record is a verified same-class variant (e.g. 'sqli-search-q').

original_pattern.description: Abstract pattern signature copied verbatim from the root finding during variant analysis.

run.description: One-line reproduction command for the operational overlay (e.g. 'bash scans/va-003-poc.sh'). Surfaced by export submission as the **Run:** header line so a re-render/--overwrite rebuilds it from the finding instead of wiping the operator's hand-applied overlay.

pass_if.description: Success criterion for the operational overlay (e.g. 'HTTP 200 returns another member's order record'). Surfaced by export submission as the **Pass if:** header line.

replies.description: Append-only thread of OUTGOING replies to the program on this submitted finding (Bugcrowd comment / HackerOne activity reply / direct follow-up). Drafts are written by `vigil assess record-reply` via read-modify-write and rendered by `export reply`; sent replies export their separate immutable byte record and are never rerendered from this authored thread.

seq.description: 1-based, monotonic reply index. export reply/record-reply pick max(seq)+1 for a new reply.

platform.description: Reply channel: bugcrowd (comment), hackerone (activity reply), or direct (reply email).

in_response_to.description: Verbatim triager ask this reply answers.

reply_to_seq.description: Optional threading pointer to a prior reply seq (default: the last reply).

body.description: Editable authored reply prose used by the exact-byte renderer at send time. After send, the immutable byte record — not this field — is the historical outbound representation.

new_evidence.description: Optional NEW proof authored for THIS reply. Preserve captured credentials, tokens, PII, and other evidence verbatim.

sent_status.description: Operator-marked send state. 'sent' is set only by `record-reply --sent` through the atomic sent-reply byte-capture endpoint, never inferred or accepted through a generic finding update.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp stamped when record-reply first created the entry.

sent_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp stamped when `--sent` marked the reply sent; null while a draft.

corrects_seq.description: Sent reply seq superseded by this appended correction version.

event_type.description: Marks an appended reply as a correction event.

correction_history.description: Retraction/correction history for this finding — quoted supersessions naming the internal slugs they retract. Rendered ONLY under OPERATOR DETAILS; never in the pasteable submission body, so naming a slug here cannot trip the export hygiene gate.

withdrawal_reason.description: Why the researcher withdrew this submission. REQUIRED when submission_status is set to 'withdrawn' — a retraction is researcher-initiated, so the record must say why rather than assert a program decision.

poc_request.description: HTTP request that triggers the vulnerability.

poc_response.description: Observed HTTP response that confirms the vulnerability.

function.description: Function or method containing the vulnerable operation.

discovery_stage.description: Code workflow stage that identified the finding.

source_anchor.description: Verbatim source expression anchoring the finding in the reviewed snapshot.

proof_complete.description: True when the code-verification path established a complete source-to-sink proof.

discovered_credential.description: Credential-store record and optional replay identity created from a discovered secret.

timeline.description: Ordered incident timeline entries, each a UTC ISO-8601 event citing its `source_file` and `command_run_id` per agent/rules/ir-evidence.md. Appended across investigation rungs, never replaced.

iocs.description: Indicators of compromise observed for this finding (IP, domain, email, file hash, OAuth client_id, URL). Each one gets an `intel_*` row via `vigil assess intel record`.

provenance.description: Typed reserved provenance with forward-compatible producer metadata.

code_snapshot.description: Immutable identity of the verified source snapshot behind a code finding.

repo_id.description: code_repos.id for the source snapshot reviewed for this finding.
repo_id.title: Repo Id

repo_generation.description: The repository active_generation reviewed for this finding.
repo_generation.title: Repo Generation

source_manifest_digest.description: The repository source_manifest_digest reviewed for this finding.
source_manifest_digest.title: Source Manifest Digest

code_snapshot.title: CodeSnapshotProvenance

agent_id.description: Dispatch agent_id of the agent that AUTHORED this finding (e.g. 'HUNT-RUN-1'), copied verbatim from its Runtime Identity block — a dispatch id, not the role name in agent_name. A true insert requires it and resolves it in the engagement. Re-recording a valid authored finding may omit it because the immutable original is preserved. Historical authorless rows require the one-time finding bind-author repair.

agent_name.description: Agent that produced this finding (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst'). Mirror of source_name.

artifact.description: Path or ID of the artifact this finding was derived from.

provenance.title: FindingProvenance

evidence_type.title: Evidence Type
evidence_type.description: Strength of evidence. 'network-confirmed': live exploit or observed response. 'code-inferred': static/dataflow analysis without runtime proof. 'theoretical': logic-based hypothesis, no code or traffic evidence. 'informational': non-exploitable observation.

submission_status.title: Submission Status
submission_status.description: External bug-bounty/program submission state, ORTHOGONAL to workflow_status (report-inclusion). 'none': not submitted. 'submitted': sent to the program. 'accepted'/'rejected'/'duplicate': program triage outcome. 'needs_info': program requested more detail. 'withdrawn': the RESEARCHER retracted the submission (requires details.withdrawal_reason; never use 'rejected' for this, which asserts a program decision that did not happen). Moving to any non-'none' value requires submission_ref. Omit to keep the default 'none'.

submission_platform.title: Submission Platform
submission_platform.description: Where the report was filed: 'bugcrowd', 'hackerone', or 'direct'.

submission_ref.title: Submission Ref
submission_ref.description: The program's own identifier for the report (e.g. a Bugcrowd submission id or HackerOne report number). REQUIRED when moving submission_status to a non-'none' value — a submission state with no referent cannot be joined back to the report it describes.

submission_url.title: Submission Url
submission_url.description: Direct URL to the filed report, when the platform exposes one.

request_variant_id.title: Request Variant Id
request_variant_id.description: ID of the request variant this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that request-variant surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific request variant.

service_id.title: Service Id
service_id.description: ID of the service this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that service surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific service.

surface_id.title: Surface Id
surface_id.description: ID of the attack surface this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific surface.

target_kind.title: Target Kind
target_kind.description: Entity type of the link target (e.g. 'finding', 'credential', 'access_record', 'attack_chain').

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: Database ID of the target entity. Provide target_id OR target_ref, not both.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description: Slug or string reference for the target when target_id is unavailable.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Why this link exists or how the two entities are related.

title: Assessment Finding Record

examples.title: Blind SQL injection in search
examples.summary: Boolean-blind SQL injection on the search endpoint

details.impact: Anonymous attackers can extract arbitrary data from the backing store
details.remediation: Use parameterized queries for all search input

examples.title: Heap buffer overflow in URL parser via overlong scheme
examples.summary: Attacker-controlled URL scheme exceeding 64 bytes overflows heap buffer in parseurl()

details.impact: Remote code execution via heap corruption
details.evidence: memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen) copies attacker-controlled bytes without a bounds check
details.taint_path: curl_url_set(CURLURLPART_URL, attacker_url) -> parseurl() -> memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen)
details.guards_evaluated: No bounds check on schemelen before memcpy
details.remediation: Add bounds check on schemelen before memcpy; reject URLs with scheme longer than 63 bytes
details.chain_rationale: The primitive is meaningful for exploitation, but final report impact depends on chaining it to a reachable crash or controlled allocation path.
required_followup: Exercise the URL parser through a network-reachable caller
Confirm whether the overflow produces controlled corruption under sanitizer instrumentation

examples.title: BFLA on role-grant endpoint (blocked: needs org-admin group)
examples.summary: The role-grant endpoint appears to lack function-level authz, but confirming it requires an account provisioned into the org-admin group.
examples.notes: Anonymous + member roles 403 at the gate; the grant call is only reachable once inside org-admin — provisioning not available this engagement.

details.impact: If confirmed, a low-privilege user could grant themselves arbitrary roles (privilege escalation).
details.evidence: GET /api/roles/grant returns 403 for member; the UI only renders the grant control for org-admin.
details.block_reason: Cannot reach the role-grant endpoint without an org-admin-group account.

unblock_requirements.description: A test account provisioned into the org-admin group with role-management entitlement.

details.attempts_summary: Tried anonymous, member, and billing-admin sessions; all 403 at the function gate. Recorded via block-technique (BFLA on this host).
